title: Measuring the Earth with a shadow? Eratosthenes did it
description:
Alexandria, around 240 BC: Eratosthenes compares the noon shadows in Syene and Alexandria – and works out the size of the entire Earth. Here's how the one-fiftieth trick works and how close he came to the real 40,000 kilometers.

One true story from the history of math – every day.
Created with AI assistance (animation and voice); facts from the sources listed.

Sources:
· Kleomedes, Meteora (Die Kreisbewegung der Himmelskörper) I.7
· MacTutor History of Mathematics, Eratosthenes of Cyrene (St Andrews)
· A. Chodos, June ca. 240 B.C.: Eratosthenes Measures the Earth, APS News (2006)
· D. Thompson, Measuring the Earth, Astronomy 161, Ohio State University
